# QM Basic: Course overview {#basic-course}

QM Basic introduces the language and logic needed to turn data into careful
evidence. We begin with data summaries and visualisation, build probability
models, and then use sampling distributions to understand confidence
intervals and two-sided tests against zero.

::: {.outcomes}
<span class="label">By the end of QM Basic, you can</span>

- identify observational units, variables, samples, populations, and
  selection limits;
- summarise and visualise quantitative and categorical data in R;
- work with events, random variables, distributions, expectation, variance,
  covariance, and correlation;
- use uniform, normal, and t models with their stated conditions;
- explain sampling variability, standard errors, confidence intervals, and
  two-sided tests against zero;
- interpret supplied R output with correct units, uncertainty, scope, and
  causal limits.
:::

## How to read every graph

Use the same sequence whenever a graph appears:

1. Read the horizontal axis: identify the variable, its units, and the shown
   range.
2. Read the vertical axis: decide whether it shows a count, proportion,
   percentage, density, outcome, residual, or fitted value.
3. Decode each mark: determine what one point, bar, line, shaded area, or
   interval represents.
4. Check the scale and displayed sample: look for zooming, unequal panel
   scales, omitted observations, and whether an axis starts at zero when that
   matters.
5. Describe the visible pattern before interpreting it. Then state the
   population, design, and causal limits.

The graph-specific paragraphs in the lectures apply this sequence directly.

## The weekly rhythm

Both QM courses run on a fixed prep--class--practice cycle with stated time
budgets. The [How to succeed in this course](../resources/how-to-succeed.qmd)
page lays out the week, day by day, with printable checklists.

## Tutorials and assessment

Four tutorials provide guided exam preparation. Bring your attempted
after-class questions and use the cumulative
[QM Basic Formula Sheet](formula-sheet.qmd) during each tutorial. The
complete sheet is attached to the closed-book written exam.

The [QM Basic Mock Exam](mock-exam.qmd) contains 100 points and uses the same
calculation, supplied-output interpretation, conditions, and scope language
required in the course.
